name: Archdiocese of New York

base: The cathedral is on the national news twice a year and the archbishop is asked about the president. Everything said from a pulpit here can be repeated in print by Monday.
The parishes run from Park Avenue to the Bronx to the far end of the Hudson, and a man can spend a whole career being moved between worlds that do not speak to each other.
The presbyterate is large, old, and multilingual, and it remembers every archbishop it has had.

byNeed.critically_short: The archdiocese is closing parishes faster than it can announce them, and a newly ordained man is a pastor before he is ready.
byNeed.stretched: Clustering and mergers are the constant subject; the personnel board meets more than it would like.
byNeed.adequate: The bench is respectable, thanks to the seminary and the foreign priests the archdiocese has always been able to attract.
byNeed.deep_bench: There are more priests than parishes that can use them well, and the wait for a pastorate is long.

byFinancial.healthy: The money is there, in endowments and in a handful of donors who expect to be called by name.
byFinancial.strained: The money is in the wrong places: rich parishes with no children and poor parishes with full schools.
byFinancial.crisis: The archdiocese has sold buildings that were never supposed to be for sale, and the settlements are not finished.

byTension.one_voice: Whatever the presbyterate thinks, it says with one voice, because the chancery has made clear what happens otherwise.
byTension.quietly_split: The presbyterate is split along lines that only show at clergy dinners, after the second bottle.
byTension.openly_divided: The presbyterate fights in the diocesan paper and in the secular one, and the archbishop is a party rather than a referee.

complications: A consolidation plan that will close a fifth of the parishes in ten years, with the list not yet public.
A tabloid with a reporter on the religion beat who has sources in the chancery.
Debt from the last capital campaign that the next one is supposed to retire.
A cathedral restoration that has run over by a figure nobody will confirm.
hiddenComplications: A vicar general who is running the archdiocese while the archbishop travels, and who intends to keep doing so.
Settlements still being negotiated from cases twenty years old, with a bankruptcy filing quietly prepared.
The seminary's rector and the archbishop have not spoken privately in a year.
